diet_tip.dilute_juice: Choose sugar-free drink / Dilute juice 1:1 with water
diet_tip.swap_dessert: Swap dessert for plain yogurt + berries
diet_tip.steam_then_sear: Steam your food first, then sear briefly
diet_tip.decouple: Decouple (eat at home first, socialize out)
diet_tip.plate_method: Use the plate method (½ veggies, ¼ protein, ¼ carbs)
diet_tip.dilute_juice_desc: Choose sugar-free drinks when possible. Avoid fruit juice if you can — they contain sugar, not fibre, so juice can cause your blood sugar to spike quickly. If you have to, limit to 150ml and dilute 1:1 with water.
diet_tip.swap_dessert_desc: Most desserts are high in refined sugar with little fibre, leading to a sharp glucose rise. Plain yogurt without sugar and berries (the ideal food for glucose control) is the perfect combo.
diet_tip.steam_then_sear_desc: Deep-frying adds significant fat calories, which over time contributes to weight gain — a key driver of insulin resistance. Steaming first cooks the food through without excess oil, so only a brief sear is needed for texture.
diet_tip.grilled_over_fried_desc: Fried foods are often coated in batter or breadcrumbs and soaked in oil, increasing the overall calorie and carbohydrate load. Grilling removes both, keeping the meal's glycaemic impact lower.
diet_tip.decouple_desc: Restaurant portions tend to be larger and higher in refined carbs than home-cooked meals. Eating beforehand means you take on little to no extra glucose load from the outing.
diet_tip.share_mains_desc: How much you eat directly determines how much glucose enters your bloodstream. Sharing dishes naturally reduces your portion without requiring willpower or calorie counting.
diet_tip.swap_sides_veggies_desc: Typical sides — chips, rice, and bread — are high in starch, which breaks down rapidly into glucose. Non-starchy vegetables are low in carbohydrates and high in fibre, producing a much smaller blood sugar response.
diet_tip.plate_method_desc: The balance of nutrients on your plate affects how quickly glucose rises after eating. Fibre from vegetables and protein both slow digestion, while limiting the carb quarter caps the total glucose load.
diet_tip.kitchen_closure_desc: Snacking at night adds carbohydrates when your body's insulin response is naturally weaker, leading to higher overnight blood sugar. Stopping food intake after dinner gives your glucose levels time to return to baseline before sleep.
diet_tip.switch_edamame_nuts_desc: Most snacks are high in refined carbs, which spike glucose quickly. Edamame and nuts are rich in protein, fibre, and healthy fats — nutrients that have minimal direct impact on blood glucose.
diet_tip.food_switch_desc: Replace part of your meal with these foods that have lower impact on glucose spike: Legumes & Pulses (kidney beans, lentils, chickpeas, split peas, soybeans, baked beans), Non-Starchy Vegetables (leafy greens, broccoli, tomatoes, raw carrots, green beans), Whole Grains & Cereals (rolled oats, barley, quinoa, buckwheat, stone-ground whole wheat bread).

welcome.title: Welcome to Glukky
welcome.p1: Glukky helps you manage blood sugar through two daily habits.
welcome.p2: A short walk after dinner. One small diet change each week.
welcome.p3: The app adapts to how you're doing. You stay in control.

diet_focus.title: How your diet focus works
diet_focus.p1: We focus on one diet area at a time — for 3 weeks.
diet_focus.p2: Each week, one simple tip to try. No full diet overhaul.
diet_focus.p3: Reach 80% follow-through over 3 weeks and you've mastered it — then we move to the next.

dinner_timing.title: Why dinner timing matters
dinner_timing.p1: Late at night, your body's insulin response weakens.
dinner_timing.p2: The same meal at 10pm raises blood sugar more than at 7pm.
dinner_timing.p3: We prioritise dinner timing over other diet habits — it has the biggest impact.
dinner_timing.p4: On nights you can't eat early, we'll give you tactics to soften the effect.

first_walk_day.title: Your first walk day
first_walk_day.p1: Here comes your first post-meal walk! A short walk after dinner is one of the most effective things you can do for blood sugar.
first_walk_day.p2: Struggling to find 10 minutes? Try natural 'excuses' — take out the rubbish, collect the mail, or buy groceries on foot.
first_walk_day.p3: Take the stairs. Add an extra loop around your building, block, or the nearby park.

stretch_switch.title: Switching to gentle stretching
stretch_switch.p1: Walking has been tough recently — that's normal.
stretch_switch.p2: We're switching to a 2-minute post-dinner stretch to keep the habit alive.
stretch_switch.p3: Once you're ready, we'll ease back into walks gradually.

walk_escalation.title: Building back to walks
walk_escalation.p1: Great consistency with stretching — that's the hard part.
walk_escalation.p2: Walking has a stronger effect on blood sugar than stretching.
walk_escalation.p3: We'll start you back at 10 minutes. You can always say "not yet".

glycemic_gap.title: The glycemic gap
glycemic_gap.p1: A long walk on Monday doesn't protect you from a spike on Tuesday.
glycemic_gap.p2: More days of walking — even short ones — matters more than longer walks on fewer days.

roadmap_progress.title: Reading your progress
roadmap_progress.p1: Your roadmap tracks walks, dinner timing, and diet tips.
roadmap_progress.p2: A 70% rate is genuinely good progress.
roadmap_progress.p3: The trend over weeks matters far more than any single week.

piggy_bank.title: Your piggy bank
piggy_bank.p1: Complete walks and follow diet tips to earn coins.
piggy_bank.p2: Reach 60 coins and claim the reward you set for yourself.
piggy_bank.p3: Pick something you genuinely want — it works better that way.

dinner_tactics.title: Your three dinner tactics
dinner_tactics.p1: Fiber Starter — eat your vegetables first. Fibre slows glucose absorption.
dinner_tactics.p2: Dusk Prep — small snack at 5pm means a smaller, less impactful late dinner.
dinner_tactics.p3: Split Dinner — two smaller meals are easier on your blood sugar than one large one.

struggle_intro_sugary.title: Sugary drinks and desserts usually cause rapid spikes in blood sugar because they are absorbed quickly.
struggle_intro_sugary.body: Pick one of our advices to improve your health and wellbeing!

struggle_intro_oily.title: Eating too much unhealthy fat can make you put on weight, which may make it more difficult to manage blood glucose levels.
struggle_intro_oily.body: Pick one of our advices to improve your health and wellbeing!

struggle_intro_portions.title: Large portion sizes (of unhealthy food) increase the total load of carbohydrate, fat and calories, making blood sugar levels and weight harder to control.
struggle_intro_portions.body: Pick one of our advices to improve your health and wellbeing!

struggle_intro_snacks.title: Snacks can either help or hurt blood sugar control depending on timing and content.

struggle_intro_eat_out.title: Eating out makes it harder to control what goes into your food — hidden oils, large portions, and sugary sauces can all push blood sugar higher.

health_info.plate_method_desc: Fill your plate using this simple guide to balance nutrients and manage blood sugar:
health_info.plate_method_tip: Filling half your plate with vegetables first slows glucose absorption and keeps you fuller for longer.
health_info.food_switch_desc: Swapping your usual snack for edamame or nuts is a simple way to reduce blood sugar spikes between meals.
health_info.food_switch_content_edamame: Edamame (young soybeans) are high in protein and fibre, and have a low glycaemic index. They digest slowly and cause a much smaller blood sugar rise than most snack foods.
health_info.food_switch_content_nuts: Nuts like almonds, walnuts, and pistachios are rich in healthy fats and protein. They slow digestion and reduce the glycaemic impact of the meal or snack that follows.
health_info.food_switch_content_why: Most packaged snacks are high in refined carbohydrates, which cause rapid blood sugar spikes. Edamame and nuts provide sustained energy without the sharp rise and fall.
health_info.food_switch_content_when: Try them as a mid-afternoon snack (around 3–4pm) or when you feel like something between meals. Eating them before a larger meal can also help blunt the overall blood sugar response.
health_info.food_switch_content_tip: Keep a small portion of nuts (about a small handful) or a bag of frozen edamame ready in your kitchen. The easier they are to reach, the more likely you are to choose them.

glucose.alert_low_body:
Take 15 g of fast-acting carbs right now: honey, fruit juice, or sugar cubes.
Wait 15 minutes, then check your glucose again.
If symptoms persist or do not improve, seek medical attention immediately.
glucose.alert_high_body:
Drink water and avoid high-sugar foods and drinks.
Seek medical attention if you notice any of the following: extreme thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, nausea or vomiting, difficulty breathing, or unusual fatigue.
glucose.alert_disclaimer: This is general self-care information only. Always follow your doctor's personal guidance.

disclaimer.onboarding: Glukky builds a personalised picture of your dietary and blood sugar patterns based on the data you log. Results reflect long-term trends, not medical diagnoses. Individual readings can be affected by stress, sleep, illness, and other factors that may not always be recorded. Please consult your doctor before making any changes to your medication or treatment plan.
disclaimer.hstix: Readings can be affected by many factors, such as stress, illness, or differences in meal timing. The more you log, the clearer your personal pattern becomes.
disclaimer.footer: The information in this app is not a substitute for medical advice.
